these first two episodes are better viewed as pt 1 and pt 2 of a whole pt 1 harper and eric pt 2 yas and henry in the first part we are introduced to new characters before quickly moving on to find out what harper is up to which sets the stage for the main plot of the season we see harper sever her relationship to otto mostyn and destroy the fund then reach out to eric to suggest a new partnership we find eric retired and feeling bored and untethered and eager to get back in the game our new tech bros are given time to establish the depth of their friendship before whitney unceremoniously kicks him out of the company thereby leaving an opening for ceo in comes henry during pt 1 we only see glimpses of yas as she plans an event and there are subtle hints that all is not well at the manor and that henrys cold is more likely his black dog returned in several instances she mentions henry and whitney possibly working together she sounds almost desperate clearly these talks have begun prior to the start of the episode we learn henry lost an election to a new character jennifer bevin also in attendance and someone whitney wants an introduction to meanwhile harper is introduced to whitney and gets to know him real quick in a very intimate way in pt 2 we now get to see what exactly yas has been up to and what her life is currently like however the episode is told through henrys eyes why henry because he will become the fulcrum for the season all characters are in some way tied to henry becoming ceo of tender a company that already has an investigative reporter on its heels this sets up the main tension between harper and yas as one will seek to destroy it while the other is using it to remain relevant it perfectly explains the poster for s4 henry is quite literally in between them tender is a great play on its meaning and its role in the story while it works perfectly to describe a payment processor a form of payment it is also the exact opposite of how whitney intends for the app to work in society a bank killer there is nothing tender about whitney we see his ruthlessness straight away yet by inserting henry into the role of ceo a character who could certainly use some tender mercies to play the poster boy for wealth and privilege it asks the viewer to humanize henry too as it does to everyone in the story we might see harper and yas and eric do some despicable things but we also see a very human side to them they all desperately need some tenderness in their lives anyway i just thought the two episodes were great companion pieces and wanted to point out that its not so much that no finance takes place in this episode so much as no finance takes place in this half of what is essentially a long episode
